rules.default_position: Provider retains all pre-existing IP; Client owns custom deliverables and receives license to use Provider IP incorporated in deliverables

acceptable_alternatives.position: Shared ownership of custom IP developed jointly
acceptable_alternatives.conditions: Only for significant client-funded R&D projects over $250k

acceptable_alternatives.position: Client owns all IP with Provider retaining portfolio rights
acceptable_alternatives.conditions: Premium pricing (20-30% increase) and explicit portfolio/reference rights
acceptable_alternatives.notes: Must negotiate case study and reference rights

unacceptable_positions.position: Client owns Provider's core frameworks and methodologies
unacceptable_positions.reason: These are StrataNoble's competitive advantage and reusable across all clients

unacceptable_positions.position: Transfer of Provider's pre-existing IP library
unacceptable_positions.reason: Pre-existing IP represents years of development investment

rules.escalation_reason: Any deviation from standard IP model requires executive approval
rules.notes_for_ai: IP ownership is a core negotiation point. Never concede Provider's pre-existing IP. Always emphasize that Client gets ownership of custom work product plus perpetual license to use Provider's tools/frameworks.

rules.default_position: Liability capped at total fees paid in preceding 12 months; no liability for consequential damages

acceptable_alternatives.conditions: Enterprise clients (>$500k deals) with appropriate insurance coverage
acceptable_alternatives.notes: Must verify we have adequate E&O insurance

acceptable_alternatives.position: Liability cap of total project value
acceptable_alternatives.conditions: Projects under $100k where risk is manageable

unacceptable_positions.reason: Exposes company to existential risk

unacceptable_positions.position: Liability for consequential damages without cap
unacceptable_positions.reason: Cannot predict or insure against consequential damages

unacceptable_positions.position: Liability cap below total project fees
unacceptable_positions.reason: Insufficient to cover actual damages; unfair allocation

rules.escalation_reason: Any cap above 1x fees requires risk assessment and insurance verification
rules.notes_for_ai: Liability limitations are critical for business survival. Never agree to unlimited liability. Always exclude consequential damages. Standard cap is fees paid in last 12 months.

rules.default_position: 50% upfront deposit, remainder on milestones; Net 15 payment terms

acceptable_alternatives.conditions: Established clients with payment history, projects over $100k
Any size client willing to accept this structure
Enterprise clients with established payment processes
acceptable_alternatives.notes: Only if deposit percentage is maintained

unacceptable_positions.reason: Necessary to secure commitment and cover setup costs
Creates excessive cash flow risk and client leverage
Insufficient to justify resource allocation

rules.notes_for_ai: Payment terms protect cash flow. Always require meaningful upfront deposit (minimum 30%, prefer 50%). Never accept payment-on-completion-only terms. Milestones should align with deliverable completion.

rules.default_position: 30-day warranty on deliverables; correction or refund as sole remedy

acceptable_alternatives.conditions: Complex projects where reasonable testing time is needed
Deals over $250k with extended testing/UAT requirements

unacceptable_positions.reason: Creates indefinite liability exposure
Cannot warrant work we didn't perform
Cannot control third-party systems

rules.notes_for_ai: Warranty should be limited in time and scope. 30 days is standard, can extend to 90 for large deals. Never warrant client modifications or third-party components. Sole remedy is correction or refund.

rules.default_position: Provider indemnifies only for IP infringement of deliverables; Client indemnifies for misuse

acceptable_alternatives.notes: Third-party components subject to their own licenses

unacceptable_positions.position: Provider indemnifies for all third-party IP claims
unacceptable_positions.reason: Cannot control or verify all third-party IP rights

unacceptable_positions.position: Indemnity not subject to liability cap
unacceptable_positions.reason: Creates unlimited exposure
Cannot control what client does with deliverables

rules.notes_for_ai: Indemnification for IP infringement is standard but must be limited. Never indemnify for third-party components, client modifications, or use cases outside scope. Indemnity should be subject to overall liability cap.

rules.default_position: Either party can terminate with 30 days notice; Client pays for work completed

acceptable_alternatives.conditions: Long-term engagements where resource planning is critical
Projects under $25k or under 3 months duration

unacceptable_positions.position: Client can terminate immediately without cause
unacceptable_positions.reason: Leaves Provider exposed with allocated resources

unacceptable_positions.position: No payment for work-in-progress on termination
unacceptable_positions.reason: Provider must be compensated for work performed

rules.notes_for_ai: Termination provisions should be mutual and balanced. Always require notice period and payment for work completed. Never accept terms that allow client to walk away without paying for performed work.

rules.default_position: Nevada law governs; disputes resolved in Nevada courts or arbitration

acceptable_alternatives.position: Client's home state law if in US
acceptable_alternatives.conditions: Large deals (>$500k) where client insists on their jurisdiction
acceptable_alternatives.notes: Prefer arbitration to mitigate forum issues

acceptable_alternatives.conditions: Common for enterprise agreements; well-established business law
acceptable_alternatives.notes: Delaware law is predictable and business-friendly

unacceptable_positions.reason: Difficult and expensive to enforce; unfamiliar legal system

unacceptable_positions.position: Jurisdiction with unfavorable IP or contractor laws
unacceptable_positions.reason: Could undermine our IP protections or create employment issues

rules.escalation_reason: Any jurisdiction change requires legal review
rules.notes_for_ai: Nevada is default but we can be flexible within the US. Prefer arbitration for dispute resolution. Foreign jurisdictions require careful review. Always confirm choice of law doesn't conflict with IP protections.

acceptable_alternatives.conditions: When dealing with true trade secrets (not just confidential info)

acceptable_alternatives.notes: Shorter term acceptable for commodity information

unacceptable_positions.reason: We also share confidential information about our methodologies
Insufficient protection period

rules.notes_for_ai: Confidentiality should be mutual. 5 years is standard, can adjust to 3-10 years based on information sensitivity. Always include standard exclusions (public domain, prior knowledge, independent development, required disclosure).

general_guidance.negotiation_approach: Collaborative problem-solving; understand client's concerns and find win-win solutions within playbook parameters
red_flags: Demands for Provider's core IP transfer

escalation_thresholds.executive_approval_required: Deals over $250k or any hard-stop violation
escalation_thresholds.legal_review_required: Foreign jurisdiction, unusual IP arrangements, uncapped liability requests
escalation_thresholds.cfo_approval_required: Payment terms more generous than 40/60 split, extended payment terms beyond Net 30
